Let \(f=(-1)^q\), where \(q:V\to \mathbb F_2\). The four-term condition says exactly that \(q\) is a quadratic refinement of \(B\):
\[
q(z+r+s)+q(z+r)+q(z+s)+q(z)=B(r,s).
\]

A convenient refinement is
\[
q_0(z)=\sum_{i=1}^m \operatorname{Tr}_{k/\mathbb F_2}(z_i^5),
\]
since in characteristic \(2\),
\[
(z+w)^5+z^5+w^5=z^4w+zw^4.
\]
Also \(q_0(Sz)=q_0(z)\), because \(\alpha^5=1\) and \(S\) only permutes coordinates after multiplying by \(\alpha\).

The form \(B\) is nondegenerate, so all refinements are
\[
q_v(z)=q_0(z)+B(z,v),\qquad v\in V.
\]
For such a quadratic sign function,
\[
\mathcal F((-1)^{q_v})(w)=\varepsilon(q_v)(-1)^{q_v(w)}.
\]
For one coordinate, \(Q(x)=\operatorname{Tr}_{k/\mathbb F_2}(x^5)\) has \(6\) zeros and \(10\) ones on \(\mathbb F_{16}\), so its normalized Gauss sign is \(-1\). Since \(m=106\), \(\varepsilon(q_0)=(-1)^{106}=1\), and
\[
\varepsilon(q_v)=(-1)^{q_0(v)}.
\]

The condition \(Tf=f\) gives, at \(0\), \(\varepsilon(q_v)=1\), hence \(q_0(v)=0\). It also requires \(q_v(Sz)=q_v(z)\), which is equivalent to \(Sv=v\).

Now count \(v\in \operatorname{Fix}(S)\) with \(q_0(v)=0\). On a cycle of length \(L\), fixed vectors exist iff \(\alpha^L=1\), i.e. \(5\mid L\). The relevant cycle lengths are
\[
5,10,15,20,25.
\]
Each contributes one free element of \(K\). For even \(L=10,20\), the contribution to \(q_0\) is \(0\). For odd \(L=5,15,25\), the contribution is \(Q(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(t^5)\).

Thus we need the number of triples in \(K^3\) with \(Q(t_1)+Q(t_2)+Q(t_3)=0\), times \(16^2\) for the two even cycles. Since \(Q\) has \(6\) zeros and \(10\) ones,
\[
\#\{Q_1+Q_2+Q_3=0\}
=\frac{16^3+(-4)^3}{2}
=\frac{4096-64}{2}
=2016.
\]
Therefore the total number is
\[
2016\cdot 16^2=2016\cdot 256=516096.
\]

\[
\boxed{516096}
\]
